latest.evidence:
Admission is a bare `used < pace` test (weekday pace, quota_ledger.go WeekdayPacePercent; +0.83pp/weekday-hour), so a run is admitted at 79.5% vs 80% and the loops flap on/off as the pace line creeps. Mark 2026-10-02: "only start if we have some headroom".
Measured (Codex weekly used_percent, from ~/.codex/sessions rate_limits, 09-26..10-02): a typical mission run costs 1-4pp (stapledon 2-3, fleet 1-2, docs 2-3, world 2-6). Outlier: World iteration 217 (10-01 18:19-23:20Z) spent +24pp in one run, 59->83, more than a full weekday's 20% pace. After it, codex was over pace; 01:27-03:15 every fire fell through to ollama/openrouter (both then exhausted, see driver:controller-fallback-skips-openrouter-ration-and-402-reads-as-crash); at 05:25 pace had crept back above used and World was re-admitted with ~1pp headroom.
Ask: (1) admission margin: start only if pace - used >= the mission's expected run cost (rolling p75 per mission+bucket from the same rate_limits data; seed 5pp for codex/anthropic until measured); otherwise yield this fire. (2) hysteresis: once a bucket is blocked, re-admit only after headroom >= that margin, not the first fire under the line. (3) in-run cap: a single run may not spend more than N pp (proposal: 10pp) of a weekly bucket; past it the controller records and exits cleanly (iter 217's 24pp would have stopped at ~69%). (4) fallback rungs are admitted with the same margin rule. Attended sessions stay ungated.

pi .pi/extensions/unowned-dirty.ts records the session's own files as ABSOLUTE paths (ownFiles.add(p.startsWith('/') ? p : `${ctx.cwd}/${p}`)) but compares them in unownedDirty() against parsePorcelain(git status --porcelain), whose paths are REPO-RELATIVE. No absolute path ever equals a relative one, so every dirty file is reported as 'did not write', including the session's own edits: the warning fires on every git add/stash/checkout and carries no signal. .pi/extensions/.unowned-dirty.test.ts only tests the pure function with relative paths (new Set(['mine.ts'])), so the wiring bug is untested. Found 2026-10-02 porting it to a Claude Code mod (M-CLAUDE-CODE-MODS V18, PR #1492). Fix: relativize own paths against git rev-parse --show-toplevel before comparing (the mod's relativeTo()), and add a wiring test. Note the mod's hooks/core.ts is generated from the pi file's pure functions (scripts/check_claude_mods_drift.sh --write) — the fix belongs in the extension wiring, so the core stays in sync.
latest.workaround: none (Claude Code port in tools/claude-mods/unowned-dirty compares repo-relative paths; pi left as-is)

Gate 5's controlplane digest send is refused on the LOCAL messaging store by the v0.52.0-17-g790169359-dirty dev CLI's new send-guard ("no agent serves 'controlplane' and it is not declared human-triage. A send here is FILED, NOT DISPATCHED"), and the driver env does NOT export AILANG_STORAGE_MESSAGING=gcp / AILANG_MESSAGES_PROJECT=ailang-multivac, which CLAUDE.md names as the canonical inbox plane for every machine doing AILANG work.

Measured 2026-10-05, world iteration 232, Gate 5:
1. `ailang messages send controlplane "<digest>" -title ... -from mission-world` (local plane, driver env) → REFUSED with the guard text above; nothing sent (rc non-zero path, message absent from the store).
2. `ailang storage status` → messaging local (default) /Users/voightkampff/.ailang/state/collaboration.db.
3. `export AILANG_STORAGE_MESSAGING=gcp AILANG_MESSAGES_PROJECT=ailang-multivac` → same send → "✓ Message sent to 'controlplane' (ID: inbox_1791218865242_707cc051)" + Pub/Sub published; body verified first-party (2,108 chars, correct title).
4. env | grep AILANG_STORAGE → not exported by the driver; tools/launchd/mission-env/mission-world.env carries no STORAGE/MESSAGING var either.
5. Historical sends to local controlplane succeeded (mission-world controlplane notifications from 2026-09-06/09-24 sit in the local store), so the guard is new in the dev binary and the loop's documented Gate-5 step now depends on an env var the driver never sets.

Workaround used: export the two documented vars before the send (CLAUDE.md § Session start). Proposed durable fix (fleet's call): export the pair from the driver (mission-base.sh / pin-root env), or declare controlplane triage in the local registry.

The log just before each crash shows the agent building a C toolchain/sysroot in /tmp (/tmp/reserved-tools/cc, CGO_ENABLED=1) and running full `make test` plus `go test ./cmd/ailang/...`. Cloud Run's /tmp is in-memory, so the test run exhausts the 8Gi and the container gets SIGBUS. Nothing was pushed before the crash, so all work was lost. The sibling sprint (M-STD-YAML-ENCODE, execution 8pldm) succeeded only because that agent abandoned full make test early.

Asks: (1) the sprint-executor skill/prompt should scope local verification to the touched packages, never install toolchains, leave the full suite to CI, and push after each milestone; (2) the executor jobs need a disk-backed scratch volume or more memory headroom for Go test caches; (3) the coordinator should mark a task failed when its Cloud Run execution fails, not 3h later.

The tasks were task-50131b05 (M-IFC-CROSS-MODULE, 1040 LOC est), task-4da1bab2 (M-MCP-FILES-FRICTION, 1180), task-06dc18ea (M-MCPHTTP-TYPED-HOST-ERRORS, 270), task-85d95401 (M-NAMED-TEST-EFFECTFUL-HELPER, 420), task-538fd63d (M-STD-YAML-MAPPING-KEY-ORDER, 200) and task-e546fce0 (M-WITH-RECV-RESERVED-WORDS, 400). Meanwhile M-EFFECT-LATENT-FUNCTION-VALUES (750) and M-IFC-AUTHORITY-SCOPING (660) finished, so size is not the main driver.

Causes, from the error text and history:
(1) The 3h clock starts at QUEUE time. With max 3 worktrees, batch dispatches spend their budget waiting.
(2) Plans required a full `make test` (slow; SIGBUS on the 8 GiB RAM-/tmp executor: crash:sprint-executor:sigbus-ram-tmp-full-make-test).
(3) The executor commits only at the end, so a timeout loses everything (also raised in sprint-evaluator:worktree-cap-and-exit1).

Asks, in priority order:
(a) Start the timeout at dispatch/start, not at queueing; report queue wait separately.
(b) sprint-planner emits ONE executor task per milestone, with a stated budget (~60-90 min); each task continues on the previous milestone's branch and STOPs at the end. The coordinator chains the next milestone task automatically, still gated by the per-sprint plan approval. The planner splits any milestone it sizes above the budget.
(c) The executor commits per milestone, and on timeout the coordinator pushes whatever commits exist and records partial progress in the sprint JSON instead of discarding the worktree.
(d) Bake focused tests (go test on touched packages + make test-core) into the planner template; never a full make test (overlaps sprint-planner:template-make-test-changelog-filesize).

Interim workaround in use: attended re-dispatch with explicit milestone slices (IFC M1-M2 only; mcp_files up to M3) and "commit after each, then STOP".

Addendum to executor:3h-timeout-from-queue-and-unsliced-sprints (2026-10-12):

Partial work is NOT preserved on timeout, and the sprint JSON does not carry progress across attempts:
- None of the 6 timed-out tasks (task-50131b05, 4da1bab2, 06dc18ea, 85d95401, 538fd63d, e546fce0) has a remote branch or PR.
- sprint_M-IFC-CROSS-MODULE.json on origin/dev is still status=not_started with M1-M4 null after two attempts. JSON progress only reaches GitHub via the final push.
- GCS artifacts for task-50131b05 and task-06dc18ea (gs://ailang-multivac-ailang-artifacts/tasks/<id>/) hold only an empty claude/projects/ prefix, 0 bytes, timestamped at dispatch. Completed tasks have transcript.txt + metrics.json. This suggests these "timeouts" may be jobs that never started (queued behind the 3-worktree cap until the queue-time clock expired), not long-running work. Please confirm from the Cloud Run job execution logs.

Additional ask: (e) if a dispatched task has not started executing within N minutes, alert or re-queue it instead of silently timing out at 3h; and expose the queue wait in `coordinator list`.

Cloud execution should mean parallel execution bounded by explicit config, not by a local disk cap (Mark, 2026-10-12: "worktrees make sense on the rig/laptop, but the idea with cloud execution is being able to do more at once").

Evidence:
- Parallelism does happen: 7 executors dispatched 2026-10-08 19:08 produced PRs from 19:11 to 21:09, overlapping, and the config comment records 13 tasks dispatched in 26s.
- But the hard-coded MaxWorktrees: 3 (internal/coordinator/daemon.go:47; enforced in daemon_tasks_exec_run.go:160 via worktreeMgr.CreateWorktree → ErrWorktreeLimitReached → reset to pending) still gates some cloud work. All six sprint-evaluator handoffs on 2026-10-08 19:11-21:09 failed "max worktrees limit reached (3)".
- Two executors from that same batch (task-06dc18ea, task-85d95401) timed out at 3h with 0-byte GCS artifacts while their siblings ran. They were held before their job began, not yet attributed.

Asks:
(a) Cloud-lane tasks (Cloud Run Job dispatch) must not take a coordinator-local worktree slot; apply MaxWorktrees only to rig/laptop/local lanes.
(b) Make max_concurrent_tasks actually govern cloud dispatch (today, per the config comment, it does not), so the per-agent throttle is explicit and honest. Raise sprint-executor/sprint-evaluator above 1 deliberately, given cost and subscription quota.
(c) Find out what held task-06dc18ea / task-85d95401 before start (Cloud Run execution records vs coordinator logs).
Related: executor:3h-timeout-from-queue-and-unsliced-sprints, executor:timeout-loses-work-and-may-never-start, sprint-evaluator:worktree-cap-and-exit1.
